comparison_details.explanation: Both images show training and test ROC curves for SVM binary classification, with true positive rate versus false positive rate, per-curve AUC annotations, and a diagonal chance baseline. Both convey strong discrimination and better overall training than test performance. However, the underlying curves and reported performance differ: reference training/test AUCs are 0.996/0.922, whereas candidate AUCs are 0.977/0.949. The candidate therefore shows weaker training discrimination, stronger test discrimination, and a smaller train-test AUC gap (0.028 versus 0.074), affecting interpretation of generalization. The candidate test curve also exceeds its training curve at some intermediate false positive rates, unlike the reference. The reference identifies cancer versus normal samples; the candidate instead specifies an RBF kernel and C=100 without identifying the outcome classes. Both satisfy the requested ROC presentation, but neither image establishes that a 70/30 split was used. Colors, typography, and dimensions do not affect this assessment. The shared evaluation structure and broad scientific message support substantial equivalence, while the numerical and curve differences prevent full equivalence.
